items.claim: The disclosed root-level echo of hll between 27:1's hitpael and 27:2's piel is byte-accurate and correctly kept as texture rather than adopted as cluster evidence.
items.evidence: collate.py byte tier confirms תִּ֭תְהַלֵּל at oshb:Prov.27.1 and יְהַלֶּלְךָ֣ at oshb:Prov.27.2 (both GREEN); the doubled-taw hitpael prefix versus the single-prefix piel yiqtol-plus-suffix form correctly marks the two as different binyanim of the same root hll, not a repeated token; skeleton comparison of the two verses (consonantal_index.json) shows no other shared content token, so no cluster evidence beyond the disclosed-and-rejected root echo exists.

items.claim: The claimed absence of any shared skeleton token between 27:7 and its neighbors 27:6 and 27:8 is confirmed.
items.evidence: Direct skeleton comparison of the three verses (consonantal_index.json) returns zero overlapping content tokens in either direction (27:6's naemanim/pitse/ohev/venatarot/neshiqot/sone shares no lexeme with 27:7's nefesh/svea/tavus/nofet/reeva/kol/mar/matoq; 27:8's katsippor/nodedet/min/qinnah/ken/ish/noded/mimqomo likewise shares none); no contained-substring or mater-lectionis trap applies to this short triad.

items.claim: The claimed absence of any shared skeleton token between 27:14 and its neighbors 27:13 and 27:15 is confirmed.
items.evidence: Direct skeleton comparison (consonantal_index.json) shows 27:14's mevarekh/reehu/beqol/gadol/babboqer/hashkem/qelalah/techashev/lo shares no token with 27:13 (qach/bigdo/ki/arav/zar/uvead/nokhriyah/chavlehu) or 27:15 (delef/tored/beyom/sagrir/veeshet/medanim/nishtavah); note 27:14 itself uses babboqer (in the morning), not beyom, so it does not share the beyom token that links 27:1 and 27:15 -- no false adjacency applies.

items.claim: The disclosed shared token ha'adam between 27:19 and 27:20 is byte-accurate in both verses, and treating it as too generic a term to bound a cluster is corroborated by its wide book-wide distribution.
items.evidence: collate.py byte tier confirms הָ֝אָדָ֗ם at oshb:Prov.27.19 and הָ֝אָדָ֗ם at oshb:Prov.27.20 (both GREEN). A word-bound sweep of the token adam and its prefixed forms (skeleton tier, consonantal_index.json, excluding the contained-substring trap where a bare substring search for adam would also catch adamah 'ground/land') returns 42 verses spread across chs 3, 6, 8, 11-12, 15-21, 23-24, 27-30 -- markedly generic next to the row's own contrast set, which is confirmed accurate: the gold-word occurs at both 25:11 and 25:12, the remove-imperative hago opens both 25:4 and 25:5, and atsel is present in all four of 26:13-26:16.

items.claim: The disclosed ketiv/qere note on the Abaddon-form at 27:20 is accurate and correctly located, and the no-cluster calls against both neighbors hold.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json kq confirms Prov.27.20:1; the source bytes show the inline-ketiv pattern directly (an unpointed form immediately followed by the pointed qere on the Abaddon word), matching the row's description precisely. Skeleton comparison against 27:21 (matsref/lakesef/vekhur/lazahav/veish/lefi/mahalalo) shows no shared token with 27:20.

items.claim: The disclosed petuchah at 27:22 and the no-shared-token claim against 27:23 are both confirmed.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json marks confirms Prov.27.22: [PE] (single-witness, tier-3, correctly labeled corroboration-only). Skeleton comparison of 27:22 (im/tikhtosh/et/haevil/bammakhtesh/betokh/hariphot/baali/lo/tasur/mealav/ivvalto) against 27:23 (yadoa/teda/pene/tsonekha/shit/libbekha/laadarim) shows zero overlap, supporting the claimed fresh start at v23.

items.claim: The row's central form claim, that 27:23 opens with the 2ms imperative pair, overstates the verse's morphology: only the second verb is a true imperative.
items.evidence: Word-split of the byte-verified source (oshb:Prov.27.23, GREEN) gives יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּ֭דַע as the first two words and שִׁ֥ית as the fifth. יָדֹ֣עַ is a Qal infinitive absolute of y-d-ʿ and תֵּ֭דַע is the Qal imperfect 2ms of the same root -- the classic infinitive-absolute-plus-cognate-imperfect emphatic construction ("you shall surely know" / "know well"), not an imperative; שִׁ֥ית alone is a genuine Qal imperative 2ms (of s-y-t, "set"). Labeling both together as one "imperative pair" -- and the device_notes' unit_type justification "given its imperative frame" -- is a translation-dependent collapse: the WEB rendering ("Know well...and pay attention...") reads as two parallel commands in English, but the Hebrew carries only one true imperative alongside one emphatic-assertion construction. This does not overturn the row's separately-argued 2ms-addressee bracketing (v23/v26/v27 possessive suffixes) or the v24 motive clause, which are independently confirmed: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א לְעוֹלָ֣ם חֹ֑סֶן byte-matches oshb:Prov.27.24 (GREEN), and its ketiv/qere note is confirmed at pmarks Prov.27.24:1, visible inline in the source bytes as an unpointed form immediately before the pointed qere on the generation-to-generation phrase -- so the admonition_unit boundary itself is not challenged, only the imperative-pair characterization feeding its rationale.

items.claim: The torah-thread claim (28:4, 28:7, 28:9, none adjacent) and the no-shared-token claims against 28:6 and 28:8 are all confirmed.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel torah restricted to ch.28 returns exactly 3 verses, 28.4, 28.7, 28.9, matching the row's enumeration and confirming no fourth occurrence was missed; the three refs are pairwise non-adjacent (gaps of 3 and 2), matching "no two torah-verses in ch.28 are consecutive". Skeleton comparison confirms 28:7 (notser/torah/ben/mevin/veroeh/zolelim/yakhlim/aviv) shares no token with 28:6 (tov/rash/holekh/betummo/meiqqesh/derakhayim/vehu/ashir) or 28:8 (marbeh/hono/beneshekh/uvetarbit/vetarbit/lechonen/dallim/yiqbetsennu); 28:8 is confirmed free of both torah and the gluttons-word zolelim.
